top.title: Four-Player Trade Proposal Sends Riley Greene to Toronto Blue Jays
top.description: The Detroit Tigers have already made several significant moves this offseason, but trading Riley Greene would take things to an entirely different level. A new trade proposal involving the Toronto Blue Jays suggests Detroit could part ways with its star outfielder in exchange for a package of four prospects. While there is no indication that the Tigers and Blue Jays are actively discussing this particular trade, the proposed return raises an interesting question about what it would take for Scott Harris to consider moving one of Detroit’s most important offensive players. Earlier this month, Harris addressed the Riley Greene trade rumors , indicating that moving the outfielder was not part of Detroit’s plans. However, that hasn’t stopped outside publications from putting together potential trade packages for the three-time All-Star. Detroit Tigers outfielder Riley Greene (31) stands in the dugout during his game against the Pittsburgh Pirates at Comerica Park in Detroit on Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Four-Player Trade Proposal Sends Riley Greene to Toronto On Friday, Victor William of Blue Jays Insider examined a three-prospect trade package originally proposed by Motor City Bengals . William suggested Toronto would likely need to include another highly regarded pitching prospect, Nolan Perry, to make the package more enticing. Here is what the hypothetical trade would look like, with prospect rankings courtesy of MLB Pipeline . Detroit Tigers receive: Nolan Perry, RHP (No. 2 prospect) Johnny King, LHP (No. 3 prospect) Blaine Bullard, OF (No. 8 prospect) Ryan Cooney, SS/2B (No. 16 prospect) Toronto Blue Jays receive: – Riley Greene, OF Perry and King would be the headliners of the deal, giving Detroit two of Toronto’s most promising young arms. Bullard would provide the Tigers with an athletic outfield prospect, while Cooney would add another young middle infielder to the organization. Should the Detroit Tigers Consider This Trade? Although acquiring four of Toronto’s top 16 prospects would certainly be intriguing, moving Greene would create an enormous hole in Detroit’s lineup. The 26-year-old outfielder hit .280 during the 2026 season and remains under team control through 2028. The Tigers recently tendered Greene a contract for 2027 , and their aggressive approach to the offseason suggests Harris is interested in building a contender rather than tearing everything down. Trading an established All-Star for four players who have yet to prove themselves at the major league level would seemingly run counter to that approach. It’s an interesting trade proposal, particularly given the upside of Perry and King, but Detroit already has something every organization covets: an established superstar entering his prime. Unless Harris receives an offer that makes the Tigers better both immediately and in the future, Greene should be staying in Detroit.

The result marks a disastrous Old Trafford debut for Mauricio Pochettino, whose side remain mired in the Premier League relegation zone after another defensive collapse. Wilson leads the charge at Old Trafford Brentford striker Wilson was the architect of Manchester United's downfall on Saturday , netting twice in a dominant first-half display that left the Old Trafford faithful in stunned silence. The experienced forward opened his account for the season in the 19th minute, showing sharp predatory instincts to ghost between two static defenders and convert Dango Ouattara's clever pass. 'It is a smaller club that does everything to the maximum of their abilities,' he said. 'Everyone on the inside feels they belong at this level. top.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers entered play on Friday with a 6-4 record and an unprecedented quarterback controversy. Earlier in the week, four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers sent head coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: either he himself call the offensive plays on the field or he was going to quit the team. McCarthy and the Steelers called his bluff, announcing that the future Hall of Famer would be benched and inactive for Friday’s game. Instead of taking the consequence, Rodgers doubled down. He went on the Pat McAfee Show and aired a great deal of grievances against McCarthy. He claimed that the head coach fell asleep in meetings, had an assistant dedicated solely to bringing him ice cream sandwiches, and that he did not have a good enough relationship with the defensive players. Pittsburgh responded by releasing Rodgers, and no NFL team wants to sign him for the home stretch of the season. In short, his career is over. Meanwhile, McCarthy is not taking the criticism lightly. top.title: Lakers schedule filled out after getting knocked out of NBA Cup
top.description: After the Lakers were knocked out of the NBA Cup , the previously unknown parts of their regular-season schedule were revealed on Friday night, featuring a first-time matchup and a familiar opponent. The league announced the Lakers will travel to Oklahoma City to play the Thunder on Dec. 6 and host the Jazz on Dec. 10 for the two games added to their schedule. The Lakers will get their first matchup against the Thunder since last season’s playoffs. Getty Images The Lakers were eliminated from the NBA Cup after Friday’s road loss to the Spurs, with the Mavericks, Trail Blazers, Grizzlies and Thunder advancing to the Knockout Rounds from the Western Conference. The Lakers-Thunder matchup will now be the first of four games between the teams, with previously scheduled games on Jan. 26 and March 6 in Los Angeles and April 1 in Oklahoma City. The Thunder, led by reigning back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, swept the Luka Doncic-less Lakers out of the playoffs in the second round in the spring to end their season before falling to the Spurs in seven games in the Western Conference finals. They’ve been without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace since the trio sustained their respective injuries against the Clippers on Oct. 25. The Lakers have a 2-1 series lead over the Jazz. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong The matchup against the Jazz and Lakers will be the fourth and final regular-season meeting between the teams. The game on Dec. 10 will be the third game in three weeks, with the Lakers falling to the Jazz on Nov. 18 to end their nine-game winning streak before beating the Jazz on Nov. 23 , with both games being in Los Angeles. The Lakers beat the Jazz on Oct. 25 in Salt Lake City for their third straight win to open the season.

top.title: 0 crosses, 0 dribbles, 1 big chance missed: Patrick Dorgu’s costly nightmare leaves Man United paying the price vs. Brentford
top.description: 0 crosses, 0 dribbles, 1 big chance missed: Patrick Dorgu’s costly nightmare leaves Man United paying the price vs. Brentford Patrick Dorgu endured a game to forget as Manchester United suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Saturday. Thrashed Mauricio Pochettino’s Old Trafford debut proved to be a nightmare as he and his players were well and truly beaten by Brentford, marking their first victory at United’s iconic home since 1937. United started brightly as they dominated possession and created chances. But they failed to make it count and were ruthlessly punished. The deadlock was broken by Callum Wilson, who gathered the ball just outside the area, spun away from United’s defenders and fired past Senne Lammens. Wilson doubled Brentford’s lead not too long after with an easy tap-in from a cross. Pochettino made changes at half-time, bringing on Luke Shaw and Bryan Mbeumo in place of Lisandro Martinez and Amad. The substitutions failed to provide any spark, as United’s response was cumbersome and fruitless. In United’s search for a breakthrough, Joshua Zirkzee lifted his effort over, Dorgu had a shot batted away, and Youri Tielemans came closest of all with an effort that clipped the crossbar. A Harry Maguire header was also stopped on the line, while substitute Shea Lacey also tested the goalkeeper with a powerful shot. But Brentford went on to secure the win in the 82nd minute as Kristoffer Ajer reacted the quickest to slam home from a corner kick. Kevin Schade then piled further misery on United with a cheeky lobbed finish. United remain in 19th place in the Premier League table and could end the matchweek at rock bottom if Crystal Palace beat Hull City on Sunday. Dorgu’s performance Pochettino elected to deploy Dorgu on the left of the attack in preference to Matheus Cunha, a decision that did not prove beneficial. Dorgu wasted several opportunities, and it could be argued that had he converted at least one, the outcome might have looked different for United. In 70 minutes on the field, Dorgu attempted three shots, just one of them on target. He ought to have done much better with the opportunity provided by Fernandes but could not get past Kelleher. He managed an individual shot accuracy of just 33.3%. found a United teammate with 14 of the 17 passes he attempted (82.4% pass accuracy). Dorgu failed to complete the one dribble he embarked on. He also did not contribute a tackle or interception. However, he won six of the eight duels he delved into. He also won three fouls. United are next in action on Wednesday when they face Newcastle at St James’ Park.

Rodri has also recovered from the hamstring injury he sustained in the win over Aston Villa on November 3. The midfielder missed Barcelona's last three matches as well as two Spain fixtures during the November international break, while Christensen returns after missing two games with a calf issue. However, the Barcelona coach must also contend with new absences, as both Alejandro Balde and Marc Bernal have been ruled out. "Rodri, Andreas and also Lamine, they travel with us and they can play," Flick told reporters. "Marc has some problems, it's not a big injury. We have to see. Alongside long-term absentees Xavi Espart and Roony Bardghji, Barcelona are also without Fermin Lopez. The midfielder is serving a two-game suspension following his red card against Villarreal last weekend, leaving Dani Olmo to step up. top.title: Kyle Whittingham contract buyout: What would firing cost Michigan?
top.description: Kyle Whittingham's contract buyout if he were to be fired at Michigan football would cost the university $24.75 million. Whittingham's future remains cloudy, with the Wolverines at 6-5 overall and 3-5 in the Big Ten standings , entering their rivalry game Saturday, Nov. 28, at unranked Ohio State . It's Michigan's worst full season since going 5-7 in 2014 , Brady Hoke's final season. Whittingham's chances of returning did not look good as recently as a week ago, when the university signed a memorandum of understanding with Trev Alberts to hire him away from Texas A&M as its new athletic director. But chaos reigns at Michigan and the university backed out of the deal by Tuesday. This has Whittingham's chances looking better to continue as coach in 2027. "The likelihood is to [keep] Kyle," one person with knowledge of the situation told the Free Press this week. "Circumstances around the AD are such that it's complicated and hard to make a change [immediately]." EXCLUSIVE: Inside Michigan AD debacle, what's next and Kyle Whittingham's future The 2027 recruiting class has early signing day scheduled for next week, Wednesday-Friday (Dec. 2-4), which makes a decision by current AD Warde Manuel, who still has authority , and others extremely pressing. Whittingham, 68, signed a five-year deal in December 2025 worth $41 million, according to his contract obtained by the Free Press as first reported on Nov. 8. Per that contract, if U-M relieves him of duties at any point during that window, he is owed an "amount equivalent to 75% of the Head Coach's Base Salary in monthly installments for the remainder of the scheduled Term of this Agreement." He's set to be paid $33 million over the next four years, which would mean a buyout would cost $24.75 million. The deal says he's required to seek immediate employment, but it's more likely this would be a retirement given his age and where he's at in his career; it's unclear how that would impact the buyout, if at all. The nearly $25 million is a drop in the bucket in the grand scheme of U-M spending, but it would be the department's latest eight-figure amount that goes toward something off the field. Michigan is still finishing payments of more than $30 million in NCAA fines for a sign-stealing scandal , recently paid more than $12 million to a law firm for an internal review of its athletic department culture , and has a athletic director search nightmare on its hands, after bungling its decision to hire Alberts, than backing out . That decision could force the university to have to pay Alberts up to $17 million and it is also on the hook to pay $4 million to buy Alberts' contract at Texas A&M, a position from which he resigned after signing with U-M. top.description: The sports world continues to pay tribute to Tom Jackson nearly a week after his death on Nov. 20 at age 75. The former Denver Broncos linebacker and longtime ESPN broadcaster built his football foundation at the University of Louisville, where he played from 1970 to 1972 before becoming a fourth-round pick in the 1973 NFL Draft. Jackson’s college roots ran deep with the Cardinals. His No. 50 jersey was honored by Louisville in 1999, recognizing a career that helped put the program on the map before his Pro Bowl and broadcasting success. That connection was on full display Saturday. top.title: Ducks Wire staff predicts Oregon Ducks vs. Washington Huskies
top.description: Rivalry week is finally here, and for the Oregon Ducks , everything is on the line. With a win over the Washington Huskies , Oregon can keep its season alive, likely grabbing a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game, or an at-large bid into the College Football Playoff, at the very least. With a loss, though, the postseason dreams would come crashing down after an awe-inspiring comeback over the past month. Talk about motivation for the Huskies to come into Autzen Stadium and ruin the party, right? To preview the game, we go through our weekly roundtable with the writers from Ducks Wire to offer our opinions and predictions for what's to come. Here is our roundtable conversation. Michigan State Reaction Question: Well, that was about as stress-free as it gets. Oregon demolished Michigan State 45-7 on Friday night, winning its fourth straight game and continuing one of the more remarkable midseason turnarounds we've seen in recent memory. What was your biggest takeaway from that win, and what impressed you most about the Ducks ' performance? Zachary Neel: I think the ability to weather an early injury was impressive. With Dierre Hill going out on the third snap of the game, Brandon Smith came in and had a career day, showing the depth of talent that the Ducks have in the backfield. A blowout win was expected over Michigan State, but the way in which the Ducks did it resonated with me. Don Smalley: I was impressed they played a complete game this time and on the road. Michigan State isn't great, but they do have the capability to bite you and Oregon never let them. Bjorn Bergstrom: My biggest takeaway was just that the Ducks looked like the Ducks: beating up on lower competition teams with ease. That’s not the Oregon squad that we saw a month ago against Illinois, but the Ducks have done it two weeks in a row against the Michigan programs. Saturday morning brought us a new day for another match where Manchester United folded under the weight of their own mistakes. Self-inflicted wounds and a pair of atrocious first half concessions put a positive opening 15 minutes to waste for the Reds. Whatever structure was established by Mauricio Pochettino going into the match was apparent with a forward-thinking approach to start the match. A better front three likely would have capitalized on the potential to create chances. Instead, it was simple saves and off-target shots and crosses. On the other end, Callum Wilson scored a brace for the visitors to kickstart their first win at Old Trafford as a Premier League side. The veteran forward scored his first with a touch past an off-balance Maguire and a shot dead center that Senne Lammens didn’t react to in time. The best shots on target came from substitute Shea Lacey having a go, demonstrating the kind of ambition and eye for making things happen that was sorely lacking from the starting group of Joshua Zirkzee, Patrick Dorgu and Amad. The three points were sealed by the visitors with a pair of dagger goals in the final minutes, ensuring another week sinking into the relegation zone for United with an Old Trafford crowd demanding change at the top. Embarrassing and weak from a once great club.

top.title: Bayern Munich’s Vincent Kompany: ‘It wasn’t a penalty’
top.description: Photo by Selim Sudheimer/Getty Images | Getty Images Bayern Munich could perhaps have squeaked a win in their away Bundesliga match against Hamburger SV. Though the team had been reduced to 10 men for the entire second half following Joshua Kimmich’s red card, they managed to stay in the game and maintain the 0-0 score line. Then, as the match entered the last minute of added time, Luis Díaz burst into the box and was brought to the ground under pressure from multiple opponents, only for the referee to judge the challenges as fair and whistle a foul against Díaz. Perhaps, on another day, the call would have been a foul on Díaz, a penalty for Bayern and a chance out of nowhere to steal all three points. If that happened, though, head coach Vincent Kompany believes it would have been the wrong call. “It wasn’t a penalty, and it wasn’t a foul against Luis Díaz,” Kompany stated plainly (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) before explaining his thinking. “There was no real contact. Why do I say it wasn’t a penalty? His foot goes into the ground, and then… you simply cannot award a penalty for something like that. No, no complaints from me. Of course, you can always have a different opinion here and there, and we certainly have ours as well. I don’t want to talk too much about it.” That penalty could have altered the course of the match late on, but Bayern and Hamburg ultimately settled for a draw after a chaotic end to the game. nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State deputy governor and incumbent senator representing Lagos West senatorial district, Dr. Idiat Oluranti Adebule has died barely 24 hours after celebrating her 56th birthday in the state. nigeria.title: Man Utd thrashed 4-0 by Brentford in Pochettino’s home debut
nigeria.description: Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 at home by Brentford on Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge to leave the 20-time English champions still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone. Callum Wilson struck a first-half double before late goals from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade sealed Brentford’s first win at Old Trafford for 89 years on Saturday. Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month, tasked with turning around the fortunes of a club in steep decline. However, the Argentine could barely have imagined a worst start after also losing 4-0 away to Liverpool in his first match in charge last weekend. For the first time in 65 years, United have conceded four goals in three consecutive league matches. That shocking defensive record has plunged the Red Devils into a battle for survival. Only Crystal Palace sit below United and Pochettino’s men could slip to the foot of the table if the Eagles beat Hull on Sunday. Pochettino came out fighting after a series of refereeing decisions went against his side against Liverpool and in a controversial 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday. But there was no hiding place for the new boss or his players after their latest embarrassment. Brentford were missing first-choice striker Igor Thiago through suspension, but it mattered little as his deputy Wilson took advantage of United’s disorganised defence. An encouraging start by the home side was quickly forgotten when Wilson lashed home a brilliant finish to open the scoring on 19 minutes. The former Newcastle and West Ham striker then doubled his tally from Dango Ouattara’s pass 13 minutes later. The end of Carrick’s reign was marked by brief flickers of United resistance in comebacks to beat Roma and salvage a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. Youri Tielemans smashed against the crossbar as United pressed for a route back into the game in the second half. But their inability to defend ended any hope of a fightback as Ajer was given way too much space to fire in from a corner. Schade then completed the rout in stoppage time as Brentford climbed to fifth and within one point of the top four. nigeria.title: 2027 : Atiku, Obi relying on regional support to win election, Shettima says

Shettima made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he questioned the opposition candidates’ campaign strategies and their efforts to build support across the country. He said Obi had visited 17 states, including all five states in the South-East and all South-South states except Rivers, but had made limited visits to other regions. According to Shettima, Obi had visited only Kaduna State in the North and Lagos State in the South-West. He also accused the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate of attempting to use religious divisions to advance his political ambition, insisting that elections could not be won through division. “You cannot win election through divisions. We win elections through negotiation, through compromises, through bridge building,” the Vice-President said. Shettima also criticised Atiku’s campaign activities, claiming that the former vice-president had visited only six states and had not travelled to any state in Southern Nigeria. “My brother Atiku Abubakar, he has so far visited six states in the Federation. He has not visited one state in Southern Nigeria. He has concentrated purely in the North,” he said. The Vice-President argued that presidential candidates needed support beyond their traditional political strongholds to secure victory, citing former President Muhammadu Buhari’s eventual success after building an alliance with the South-West. He said Buhari’s support in the North alone had not been enough to secure the presidency until he formed an alliance with the South-West. nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) mock accreditation and voting exercise in selected polling units in Kebbi State on Saturday recorded low voter turnout, although the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines operated without reported malfunctions. The exercise witnessed a predominantly female turnout, with relatively few male voters seen at several polling units visited. At Aliero Housing Estate 006 Primary School polling unit, female voters turned out for accreditation, while only a few male voters were sighted. Security personnel, including officers of the Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and State Security Service (SCIB), were deployed to provide security during the exercise. INEC ad hoc staff at the polling unit confirmed that the BVAS machines were functioning effectively during voter authentication. A visit to Gwadangaji 001 polling unit also showed a low turnout, with a few female voters presenting themselves for accreditation and no male voters sighted at the time. The voters were seen checking their names on the lists displayed on the walls before proceeding with the exercise. However, at Justice Ibrahim Umar polling unit in the GRA NEPA area, a relatively large number of female voters turned out for the mock exercise. The ad hoc staff confirmed that the two BVAS machines provided for the polling unit were working effectively, adding that no malfunction had been recorded since the exercise commenced at 9 a.m. Meanwhile, an APC stakeholder, Alhaji Abubakar ABK, described the exercise as impressive and peaceful. He attributed the participation of female voters to what he described as the humanitarian interventions of Governor Idris, expressing optimism that voters would turn out in large numbers during the January 2027 general elections. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s reforms push Nigeria’s foreign reserves to $54.13bn – City Boy Movement
nigeria.description: The City Boy Movement has hailed the rise in Nigeria’s gross foreign reserves to $54.13 billion, describing the development as evidence of progress under President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform agenda. The group said the reserves had reached their second-highest level on record since 1999, surpassed only by the $62.08 billion peak recorded in September 2008, when the global financial crisis was unfolding. In a statement titled, “Why Tinubu 4+4? Foreign Reserves Edition,” the movement said Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased significantly under the Tinubu administration, rising from $32.29 billion in May 2023 to $54.13 billion in November 2026. It put the increase at $21.84 billion, representing nearly 68 per cent growth since the President assumed office. According to the group, the latest figures place Nigeria’s foreign reserves above the peak levels recorded in several years, including 2009, 2007, 2013, 2018, 2025, 2019, 2012 and 2014. The movement noted that Nigeria’s reserves peaked at $53.25 billion in 2009, $51.33 billion in 2007, $48.86 billion in 2013 and $47.87 billion in 2018. It added that the $54.13 billion recorded in 2026 represented the highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis. While acknowledging the difficulties associated with the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, the group argued that the latest reserve figures indicated that the policies were beginning to yield positive results. It said the growth in foreign reserves was an important development in assessing the direction of the economy, expressing optimism that the country was moving towards greater economic prosperity. “The significance is in the history. Even though the reforms have been difficult, the numbers are beginning to tell their own story. We are on the way to prosperity,” the statement said. The movement also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for what it described as progress in the management of the country’s external reserves, reaffirming its support for the President. The figures cited by the group were attributed to data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). However, the movement’s assessment comes amid continuing public debate over the impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly their effects on inflation, living costs, businesses and household welfare. While higher foreign reserves can strengthen a country’s capacity to meet external obligations and support confidence in its economy, the extent to which the increase translates into improved living conditions remains a key measure of the overall success of the reforms. nigeria.description: By Chinedu Adonu The nationwide mock accreditation exercise recorded a poor turnout in most polling centres in Enugu State on Saturday, with as few as two voters accredited by the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) in some centres as of 12 noon. A correspondent who monitored the exercise observed that the low turnout could be attributed to poor public awareness, late arrival of Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ad hoc staff and difficulties encountered by some voters in locating their designated polling units. The exercise also coincided with the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Enugu State. At polling centres in Igbariam, Idaw River and Obiagu, among others, INEC ad hoc staff were observed arriving between 9:30 a.m. and 10 a.m., raising concerns about the late commencement of the exercise. Speaking at the Obiagu polling centre, a community leader, who identified himself simply as Mr Friday, attributed the poor turnout partly to the presidential visit. He said many residents had left their homes to receive President Tinubu at Okpara Square. According to him, those who turned out to welcome the President cut across party lines, as members of the APC and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), under the Rainbow Coalition, trooped out in large numbers. “So, it is clear that very few voters are currently around for the exercise, and most are not even aware or mobilised by local political leaders to participate,” he said. Also speaking, a resident of Achara Layout, Mr Arinze Madu, said he had visited two designated polling centres in search of his polling unit but had yet to locate his name. “There is little awareness to enable people know the designated polling units for the exercise in this Registration Area (RA), which is also a ward,” Madu said. Efforts to reach INEC’s Resident Electoral Commissioner in Enugu State, Dr Chukwuemeka Chukwu, for comments on the poor turnout and late arrival of electoral officials were unsuccessful, as calls to his mobile phone were not answered. nigeria.title: Apathy mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Abia
nigeria.description: …Voter alleges demand for N1m to participate By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Voter apathy marred the mock accreditation and result-upload exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Abia State on Saturday, with several polling units recording zero or minimal turnout. At Ibeku High School, one of the designated polling centres, Vanguard observed at about noon that no voter had turned up, while INEC officials waited for participants. A staff member of YIAGA Africa, who was monitoring the exercise, was also sighted at the centre but declined to comment. The situation was similar at School Road Primary School and Ugba Primary School, where electoral officials were on ground but voters were absent. Voters fault poor publicity, limited coverage At St. Stephen’s Primary School, Umuahia, however, some residents who turned out expressed disappointment that the exercise was restricted to selected polling units, blaming inadequate publicity for the low participation. Chimwe Kanu, a public servant, said she was excited about participating until she discovered that her polling unit was not among those selected for the exercise. “I’m happy to be here and to do the needful, but coming here, nothing is really happening because I was unable to vote or be captured. My polling unit is not part of the polling units selected. “I’m very disappointed because the happiness I came with, I didn’t see it again,” she said. Kanu said many prospective participants left after discovering that the exercise was limited to designated polling units. She urged INEC to improve its preparations for the 2027 general elections, particularly by ensuring the timely distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). “Many don’t have their voters’ cards. Their names are here, but their voters’ cards have not been given to them. They should make sure they share the voters’ cards as soon as possible. People need their voters’ cards,” she said. She also called on the commission to ensure early arrival of election officials and seamless accreditation of eligible voters, expressing hope that it would conduct credible elections in 2027. Similarly, Mike Uche criticised the publicity for the exercise, saying many residents arrived at polling centres unaware that participation was restricted to designated units. He said inadequate sensitisation left many confused and frustrated, alleging that some prospective participants demanded financial inducements before agreeing to take part in the exercise. Uche urged INEC to intensify voter education through radio announcements, community outreach and street sensitisation to improve participation and enlighten the electorate on the purpose of such exercises. “People are eager to come out and do the mock accreditation. They didn’t give the proper publicity,” he said, adding that participation should not be reduced to financial demands. nigeria.title: Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Katsina
nigeria.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina Low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Katsina State on Saturday ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vanguard monitoring of the exercise at Star Election Polling Unit, Wakilin Kudu 1, Kofar Gidan Iro Isansi, Rafin Dadi, showed that only a few voters turned out to participate, although some were successfully accredited. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. The mock accreditation exercise is designed to test the functionality of the accreditation system, assess the preparedness of electoral officials and identify possible technical and operational challenges ahead of the actual elections. At the polling unit, the participation of the few voters provided an opportunity to observe the practical application of the accreditation process and assess the readiness of electoral personnel. The development also highlighted the need for increased public enlightenment to ensure that eligible voters understand the purpose and significance of such exercises. Adequate sensitisation is considered essential to encouraging participation in mock exercises, which enable electoral authorities to test arrangements and address possible challenges before the main elections. The exercise also provides an opportunity to identify operational gaps and resolve potential difficulties that could affect the smooth conduct of the 2027 general elections. INEC is expected to strengthen public enlightenment and stakeholder engagement to improve awareness and encourage greater voter participation in subsequent electoral exercises. business.title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. business.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). sports.title: Four-Player Trade Proposal Sends Riley Greene to Toronto Blue Jays
sports.description: The Detroit Tigers have already made several significant moves this offseason, but trading Riley Greene would take things to an entirely different level. While there is no indication that the Tigers and Blue Jays are actively discussing this particular trade, the proposed return raises an interesting question about what it would take for Scott Harris to consider moving one of Detroit’s most important offensive players. Earlier this month, Harris addressed the Riley Greene trade rumors , indicating that moving the outfielder was not part of Detroit’s plans. However, that hasn’t stopped outside publications from putting together potential trade packages for the three-time All-Star. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Four-Player Trade Proposal Sends Riley Greene to Toronto On Friday, Victor William of Blue Jays Insider examined a three-prospect trade package originally proposed by Motor City Bengals . Here is what the hypothetical trade would look like, with prospect rankings courtesy of MLB Pipeline . Detroit Tigers receive: Nolan Perry, RHP (No. 2 prospect) Johnny King, LHP (No. 3 prospect) Blaine Bullard, OF (No. 8 prospect) Ryan Cooney, SS/2B (No. 16 prospect) Toronto Blue Jays receive: – Riley Greene, OF Perry and King would be the headliners of the deal, giving Detroit two of Toronto’s most promising young arms. The Tigers recently tendered Greene a contract for 2027 , and their aggressive approach to the offseason suggests Harris is interested in building a contender rather than tearing everything down. Trading an established All-Star for four players who have yet to prove themselves at the major league level would seemingly run counter to that approach. It’s an interesting trade proposal, particularly given the upside of Perry and King, but Detroit already has something every organization covets: an established superstar entering his prime. Unless Harris receives an offer that makes the Tigers better both immediately and in the future, Greene should be staying in Detroit.

sports.title: 0 crosses, 0 dribbles, 1 big chance missed: Patrick Dorgu’s costly nightmare leaves Man United paying the price vs. Brentford
sports.description: 0 crosses, 0 dribbles, 1 big chance missed: Patrick Dorgu’s costly nightmare leaves Man United paying the price vs. Brentford Patrick Dorgu endured a game to forget as Manchester United suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Saturday. Thrashed Mauricio Pochettino’s Old Trafford debut proved to be a nightmare as he and his players were well and truly beaten by Brentford, marking their first victory at United’s iconic home since 1937. United started brightly as they dominated possession and created chances. But they failed to make it count and were ruthlessly punished. The deadlock was broken by Callum Wilson, who gathered the ball just outside the area, spun away from United’s defenders and fired past Senne Lammens. Wilson doubled Brentford’s lead not too long after with an easy tap-in from a cross. Pochettino made changes at half-time, bringing on Luke Shaw and Bryan Mbeumo in place of Lisandro Martinez and Amad. The substitutions failed to provide any spark, as United’s response was cumbersome and fruitless. In United’s search for a breakthrough, Joshua Zirkzee lifted his effort over, Dorgu had a shot batted away, and Youri Tielemans came closest of all with an effort that clipped the crossbar. A Harry Maguire header was also stopped on the line, while substitute Shea Lacey also tested the goalkeeper with a powerful shot. But Brentford went on to secure the win in the 82nd minute as Kristoffer Ajer reacted the quickest to slam home from a corner kick. Kevin Schade then piled further misery on United with a cheeky lobbed finish. United remain in 19th place in the Premier League table and could end the matchweek at rock bottom if Crystal Palace beat Hull City on Sunday. Dorgu’s performance Pochettino elected to deploy Dorgu on the left of the attack in preference to Matheus Cunha, a decision that did not prove beneficial. Dorgu wasted several opportunities, and it could be argued that had he converted at least one, the outcome might have looked different for United. In 70 minutes on the field, Dorgu attempted three shots, just one of them on target. He ought to have done much better with the opportunity provided by Fernandes but could not get past Kelleher. He managed an individual shot accuracy of just 33.3%. found a United teammate with 14 of the 17 passes he attempted (82.4% pass accuracy). Dorgu failed to complete the one dribble he embarked on. He also did not contribute a tackle or interception. However, he won six of the eight duels he delved into. He also won three fouls. United are next in action on Wednesday when they face Newcastle at St James’ Park.

sports.title: Kyle Whittingham contract buyout: What would firing cost Michigan?
sports.description: Kyle Whittingham's contract buyout if he were to be fired at Michigan football would cost the university $24.75 million. Whittingham's future remains cloudy, with the Wolverines at 6-5 overall and 3-5 in the Big Ten standings , entering their rivalry game Saturday, Nov. 28, at unranked Ohio State . It's Michigan's worst full season since going 5-7 in 2014 , Brady Hoke's final season. Whittingham's chances of returning did not look good as recently as a week ago, when the university signed a memorandum of understanding with Trev Alberts to hire him away from Texas A&M as its new athletic director. But chaos reigns at Michigan and the university backed out of the deal by Tuesday. This has Whittingham's chances looking better to continue as coach in 2027. "The likelihood is to [keep] Kyle," one person with knowledge of the situation told the Free Press this week. "Circumstances around the AD are such that it's complicated and hard to make a change [immediately]." EXCLUSIVE: Inside Michigan AD debacle, what's next and Kyle Whittingham's future The 2027 recruiting class has early signing day scheduled for next week, Wednesday-Friday (Dec. 2-4), which makes a decision by current AD Warde Manuel, who still has authority , and others extremely pressing. Whittingham, 68, signed a five-year deal in December 2025 worth $41 million, according to his contract obtained by the Free Press as first reported on Nov. 8. Per that contract, if U-M relieves him of duties at any point during that window, he is owed an "amount equivalent to 75% of the Head Coach's Base Salary in monthly installments for the remainder of the scheduled Term of this Agreement." He's set to be paid $33 million over the next four years, which would mean a buyout would cost $24.75 million. The deal says he's required to seek immediate employment, but it's more likely this would be a retirement given his age and where he's at in his career; it's unclear how that would impact the buyout, if at all. The nearly $25 million is a drop in the bucket in the grand scheme of U-M spending, but it would be the department's latest eight-figure amount that goes toward something off the field. Michigan is still finishing payments of more than $30 million in NCAA fines for a sign-stealing scandal , recently paid more than $12 million to a law firm for an internal review of its athletic department culture , and has a athletic director search nightmare on its hands, after bungling its decision to hire Alberts, than backing out . That decision could force the university to have to pay Alberts up to $17 million and it is also on the hook to pay $4 million to buy Alberts' contract at Texas A&M, a position from which he resigned after signing with U-M. sports.title: Bayern Munich’s Vincent Kompany: ‘It wasn’t a penalty’
sports.description: Photo by Selim Sudheimer/Getty Images | Getty Images Bayern Munich could perhaps have squeaked a win in their away Bundesliga match against Hamburger SV. Though the team had been reduced to 10 men for the entire second half following Joshua Kimmich’s red card, they managed to stay in the game and maintain the 0-0 score line. Then, as the match entered the last minute of added time, Luis Díaz burst into the box and was brought to the ground under pressure from multiple opponents, only for the referee to judge the challenges as fair and whistle a foul against Díaz. Perhaps, on another day, the call would have been a foul on Díaz, a penalty for Bayern and a chance out of nowhere to steal all three points. If that happened, though, head coach Vincent Kompany believes it would have been the wrong call. “It wasn’t a penalty, and it wasn’t a foul against Luis Díaz,” Kompany stated plainly (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) before explaining his thinking. “There was no real contact. Why do I say it wasn’t a penalty? His foot goes into the ground, and then… you simply cannot award a penalty for something like that. No, no complaints from me. Of course, you can always have a different opinion here and there, and we certainly have ours as well. I don’t want to talk too much about it.” That penalty could have altered the course of the match late on, but Bayern and Hamburg ultimately settled for a draw after a chaotic end to the game. sports.title: Mercedes reveal secret behind commanding Qatar GP performance
sports.description: Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord is hoping Kimi Antonelli and George Russell can capitalise on what has been a dominant weekend for the Silver Arrows so far, with the pair once again comfortably clear of the competition in FP3 at the Qatar Grand Prix. Having dominated proceedings on Friday, Mercedes appeared equally untouchable on Saturday during FP3, with Max Verstappen emerging as the best of the rest, half a second adrift of newly crowned world champion Antonelli, who looked particularly comfortable through the high-speed corners of the Lusail circuit. All signs point towards a potential Mercedes front-row lockout in qualifying, reminiscent of the early stages of the season, when Russell and Antonelli regularly found themselves battling each other for pole position. Lord urges Mercedes to deliver when it matters in Qatar Speaking to Sky Sports at the end of FP3, Lord stressed the importance of carrying that momentum into qualifying and Sunday's Grand Prix, having failed to capitalise on Mercedes' potential in recent weekends. “It’s looked pretty good so far. We’ve done it in all the sessions that don’t matter, and now we’ve got to go out and do the job when it counts in qualifying and then tomorrow in the Grand Prix. “The last couple (of weekends) haven’t really come together. We’ve been in position to be on the podium or winning the races and haven’t done so.” Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Lord also explained why the characteristics of the Lusail circuit appear to suit the Mercedes so well, particularly compared to some of the corners in Brazil and Las Vegas. “Here, there are lots of high and medium speed corners, the car’s clearly very comfortable there. Smooth tarmac, and both drivers performing very, very strongly. “It certainly seems to suit us. The car’s been a bit weaker in the slow speed, as we saw in Vegas, as we saw in some parts of the circuit in Brazil. So, it’s playing to our strengths, but both drivers are doing a really good job with it.” Mercedes also appeared to have the upper hand over its rivals during Friday's long runs, although Sunday's Grand Prix will present an unusual strategic challenge. sports.title: Benching Austin Jackson Is The Only Move Left For Miami
sports.description: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins sit at 1-9 and need to make a bold move. Austin Jackson is not the answer at right tackle anymore. He has missed time due to injury and played inconsistently all season. The team has new options ready to step in. Head coach Jeff Hafley said Jackson has performed worse this season than in previous years. General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan wants a tough, physical line built from the inside out. Sullivan identified Patrick Paul and Aaron Brewer as the core players for this future. He also drafted Kadyn Proctor to play right tackle but moved him to left guard. Now, the door is open to switch Proctor back to right tackle. The Dolphins traded for Caeden Wallace as a swing tackle, yet he has been inactive in recent games. Starting Wallace or Proctor makes sense when the team has nothing to lose. The Case for a Change Jackson was expected to be a cornerstone player when he got drafted in 2020. Instead, he has become a liability on the offensive line. The Dolphins could not even trade him at the deadline for a future late-round pick. That shows the rest of the NFL does not value him highly. He knows he might not be on the team next year. Sitting him now gives the front office a clear look at what they have for the future. Due to knee and elbow injuries, Jackson has been limited in practice, according to Yahoo Sports . “Like most players there are bumps and bruises he is battling through,” Hafley said. “He’s doing everything he can to get ready to play.” But being ready does not mean playing well. The team needs to see if the younger guys can handle the pressure better than a struggling veteran. Jackson was downgraded to DNP on Friday’s final report. Who Steps In Next? If the Dolphins move Proctor to right tackle, they leave left guard open. The team features Jarrett Kingston, who has played well whenever they called on him. They also keep DJ Campbell on the practice squad, a player they drafted themselves. These options are worth a shot. The team can fill the open roster spot with veterans like Ronnie Harrison, who is in consideration to be activated. This is a time to test the depth and find the right pieces. Jeff Hafley said, according to Orlando Sentinel , “We’ll figure out who exactly that starter is going into Sunday.” The Dolphins face the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET at Hard Rock Stadium.

The San Antonio Spurs star is absolutely unstoppable on his day, and he is the kind of player others would be desperate to play with during their careers. Wembanyama, however, has admitted now that he wants to be teammates with one Spurs player until the day he retires. Victor Wembanyama hopes he can spend the rest of his career with Stephon Castle Wembanyama made the headlines against the Los Angeles Lakers by scoring 25 points and recording 16 rebounds, four steals, two assists and two blocks on Friday. The Frenchman was absolutely brilliant once again, but his teammate, Stephon Castle, impressed everybody with his performance as well. The 22-year-old outscored Wembanyama by a point, while also recording nine assists, four rebounds, two steals and a block in his 36 minutes on the floor. Castle was outstanding, and Wembanyama, while showering praise on him after the game, claimed that he wants to spend the rest of his career on the same team as him. science.title: How moon dust and recycled cardboard could help NASA build its lunar base
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

The high cost of building on the moon has led to wide-ranging research on how to make use of the moon's most plentiful resource: the dusty regolith that covers its surface. Right now, lunar shipping runs about $544,000 per pound ($1.2 million per kilogram), so anything that astronauts can make on the moon using existing materials could help a lot. Scientists have already proposed using regolith for building 3D-printed bricks , solar arrays , and even as soil to grow potatoes . Now, a team of researchers from Purdue University in Indiana have developed an aerogel made from simulated regolith for insulating lunar habitats. New aerogels created by Purdue University researchers, made of cellulose and lunar regolith simulant, could pave the way for insulating materials made on the moon. (Image credit: Purdue University photo/John Underwood) "Sustaining a long-term presence on the moon will require us to rethink how we use local resources," Wei, professor in Purdue's James Tarpo Jr. and Margaret Tarpo Department of Chemistry, said in a Nov. 19 statement . NASA has said that it wants a long-term, sustainable moon base up and running by 2032, a goal it aims to achieve via its Artemis program . "Rather than relying on Earth to supply everything we need, we're exploring how materials already available on the moon, including waste generated by its inhabitants, could be upcycled into something essential for safe and livable habitats," Wei said. The aerogel that the Purdue researchers have been working on is a mix of fiber from cardboard waste, called cellulose, and a material that simulates regolith. They said that it could protect the people living in habitats from the moon's drastic temperature swings. "Imagine an aerogel as a high-tech thermos for a lunar base," Jacob Staker, a graduate researcher working on the study, said in the same statement. "Most of it consists of empty space that insulates the interior, helping it maintain the temperature of what's inside." The idea here is not to create the best aerogel possible, Wei said, but that "we're looking for the sweet spot where we can get the properties we need with the limited resources we have available" on the moon. The research was published in September in the journal ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 28, 1967: Astronomers Jocelyn Bell and Antony Hewish disover the 1st pulsar with Little Green Men 1 signal
science.description: null On November 28, 1967, astronomers found the first pulsar. A pulsar is a super-dense star that rotates super fast. As the pulsar spins, it emits two beams of light in opposite directions. When astronomers look at a pulsar, it looks like a star that's flickering on and off at a steady, constant pace. The first pulsar was observed by Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish. They were looking at the constellation Vulpecula when they saw a star flickering with regular pulses separated by 1.33 seconds. At first they had no idea what it was, so they jokingly nicknamed the signal Little Green Men 1. After more pulsars were discovered, they were able to rule out aliens. This chart tracked the signal of the first pulsar ever discoverered on Nov. 28, 1967. (Image credit: Cambridge University Library/Wikipedia) Why it mattered Pulsars are naturally occurring phenomena, and they can be handy tools for astronomers . For example, some pulsars are extremely accurate clocks. Because pulsars rotate, their emission of beams of radiation is observed at regular intervals. Until Burnell's discovery, astronomers did not know if neutron stars existed, let alone if they could be observed. "Suddenly, it turned out that nature has provided an incredibly precise way to observe these objects, something that has led to many later advances," said Edward Witten, chairman of the selection committee for the Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize, which in 2018 was awarded to Burnell . Among other applications, the observation of pulsars are one of the best ways astronomers have for testing Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity. The spinning stars have also been used as a navigation tool for spacecraft moving out beyond low Earth orbit. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

According to previews provided by the department store chain, the founder of the New York City holiday celebration, space fans turning up or tuning in to catch sight of an astronaut or other nod to NASA will have only a returning rocket to look forward to on Saturday (Nov. 28). (The parade has been postponed two days from Thursday, Nov. 26, due to bad weather.) Not that Macy's (or the space agency) has hinted about anything cosmic planned for the 100th parade; it's only that the event has had a long history of celebrating space exploration with its floats and balloons. "For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . Weighty weightless man The earliest space-themed feature of the parade may have been the "Space Ship," a float that made its first appearance in the 19th procession in 1945 and in various configurations — with and without astronauts and planets — appeared on and off through 1962. Perhaps more memorable, though, and certainly much larger, was the "Spaceman" (or, more appropriately, "The Giant Spaceman"). The 70-foot-long (21-meter) helium balloon made its debut in 1952, nine years before the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. Described by Macy's as an "artist's conception of a visitor from another planet," the humanoid figure had a black spacesuit , a silver helmet and boots, a jet propulsion backpack and a black rocket gun. Once the heaviest balloon in the parade, the "Spaceman" was created by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company years before anyone had entered space. (Image credit: Macy's) Ironically, for a figure garbed for the weightless environment of space, the Spaceman was for a long time the parade's heaviest giant balloon. science.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
science.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. However, rather than having to go to the Kuiper Belt to sample the water-ice there, dust grains can bring a little bit of the Kuiper Belt to us. T

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.
